_**The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time**_ is a 2003 [mystery novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_novel "Mystery novel") by English writer [Mark Haddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Haddon "Mark Haddon"). Haddon and _The Curious Incident_ won the [Whitbread Book Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitbread_Book_Awards "Whitbread Book Awards") for Best Novel and Book of the Year,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-costabookawards-1) the [Commonwealth Writers' Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Writers'_Prize "Commonwealth Writers' Prize") for Best First Book,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-vic-2) and the [Guardian Children's Fiction Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian_Children's_Fiction_Prize "Guardian Children's Fiction Prize").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-prize2003-3)

Haddon considered this his first novel for adults, as his previous books were for children. Unusually, his publisher also released a separate edition for the children's market, and it was successful there.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Ezard-4)

The novel is narrated in [first-person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-person_narrative "First-person narrative") by Christopher John Francis Boone, a 15-year-old boy who is described as "a mathematician with some behavioural difficulties" living in [Swindon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon "Swindon"), Wiltshire. Although Christopher's condition is not stated, the book's blurb refers to [Asperger syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asperger_syndrome "Asperger syndrome"). Some commentators have characterized Christopher as on the [autism spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autism_spectrum "Autism spectrum").

In July 2009, Haddon wrote on his blog that "_The Curious Incident_ is not a book about Asperger's... if anything it's a novel about difference, about being an outsider, about seeing the world in a surprising and revealing way. The protagonist, being neuro-diverse shows that. The book is not specifically about any specific disorder". Haddon said that he is not an expert on the autism spectrum or Asperger's syndrome.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-mh-autism-5)

He chose to indicate chapters by [prime numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_number "Prime number"), rather than the conventional successive numbers, to express a different world view. Originally written in English, the book has been translated into 36 additional languages.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-translations-6)

The book’s title is a line of [Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock_Holmes "Sherlock Holmes")’ dialogue from the short story "[The Adventure of Silver Blaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Adventure_of_Silver_Blaze "The Adventure of Silver Blaze")" by [Sir Arthur Conan Doyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Conan_Doyle "Arthur Conan Doyle").

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In late 1998, Christopher John Francis Boone is a 15-year-old boy living in [Swindon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon "Swindon"), England with his widowed father, Ed. One night, Christopher discovers that his neighbour Eileen Shears' dog, Wellington, has been fatally speared with a garden fork. As Christopher mourns over Wellington's body, Eileen calls the police. When a policeman grabs Christopher's arm, Christopher panics and hits him; he is subsequently arrested for assault, though he is quickly released with a caution. Christopher decides to investigate Wellington's death and chronicle his findings in a book, despite Ed's objections. During the investigation, he meets the elderly Mrs. Alexander, who informs Christopher that his late mother Judy was having an affair with Eileen's husband Roger.

Ed discovers the book and confiscates it. While searching Ed's room for the book, Christopher finds letters from Judy, dated after her supposed death. Eventually, he realizes that Judy is still alive and living in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") with Roger. Finding a distressed Christopher in a [catatonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catatonic "Catatonic") state and realizing that he has discovered the letters, Ed admits to lying about Judy's death and confesses to killing Wellington in a fit of anger after an argument with Eileen. Fearing for his own safety, Christopher decides to run away and live with Judy.

After a long, event-filled journey, evading policemen and feeling overwhelmed by the trains and crowds around him, Christopher eventually finds his way to the home of Judy and Roger, much to the delight of the former and chagrin of the latter. Soon after arriving, Christopher requests to return to Swindon to take his mathematics [A-level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-level "A-level"), but Judy contacts the school to postpone it. She and Roger later break up due to the latter's reluctance to accept Christopher. Judy subsequently returns to Swindon with Christopher, and the exam is reinstated.

After an argument, Judy agrees to let Ed see Christopher for brief daily visits. Christopher remains apprehensive of his father, hoping he will be imprisoned for killing Wellington. Ed gifts Christopher a puppy, whom Christopher names Sandy, and promises to gradually regain Christopher's trust. Christopher declares that he will take further exams and attend university. He completes his mathematics A-level with top grades. The book ends with Christopher optimistic about his future.

## Themes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Themes")]

### Social disability

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Social disability")]

In a 2004 interview, Haddon said

> I have to say honestly that I did more research about the London Underground and the inside of Swindon Railway Station, where some of the novel takes place, than I did about Asperger's syndrome. I gave [Christopher] kind of 9 or 10 rules that he would live his life by, and then I didn't read any more about Asperger's because I think there is no typical person who has Asperger's syndrome, and they're as large and diverse a group of people as any other group in society. And the important thing is that I did a lot of imagining, that I did a lot of putting myself into his shoes in trying to make him come alive as a human being rather than getting him right, whatever that might mean.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-NPR-7)

Haddon states on his website that, although he had read "a handful of newspaper and magazine articles about, or by, people with Asperger's and autism" in preparation for writing the book, he knows "very little" about Asperger's syndrome and that Christopher Boone is inspired by two different people. According to Haddon, neither of these people can be labelled as having a disability. Haddon added that he "slightly regret[s]" that the term _Asperger's syndrome_ appeared on the cover of his novel.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-mh-autism-5) In 2010, in an interview with _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Independent "The Independent")_, he was described as

> now thoroughly irritated that the word Asperger's appeared on subsequent editions of the novel, because now everyone imagines that he is an expert and he keeps getting phone calls asking him to appear at lectures.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Independent-8)

In a critical essay on the novel, Vivienne Muller quotes some praise by experts on [disability theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disability#Theory "Disability"):

> In its presentation of Christopher's everyday experiences of the society in which he lives, the narrative offers a rich canvas of experiences for an ethnographic study of this particular cognitive condition, and one which places a positive spin on the syndrome. The reader in this instance acts as ethnographer, invited to see what Mark Osteen claims is a 'quality in autistic lives that is valuable in and of itself'.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-9) Along similar lines, [Alex] McClimens writes that Haddon's novel is 'an ethnographic delight' and that 'Haddon's achievement is to have written a novel that turns on the central character's difference without making that difference a stigmatising characteristic.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-10)

Muller adds that the novel

> works with a strong sense of the disabled speaking subject, drawing readers into Christopher's cognitive / corporeal space through an incremental layering of his perspectives and reactions... The narrative also bristles with diagrams, maps, drawings, stories, texts that inform Christopher's lexicon for mapping meaning in a world of bewildering signs and sounds.

She also admires such elements as

> the digressive stream-of-connectedness-and-disconnectedness way in which Christopher writes and thinks; the obsessive focus on minutiae; his musings about why animals behave the way they do; his quasi-philosophizing on death and life and the afterlife; his ambition to be an astronaut...[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-11)

In a survey of children's books which "teach about emotional life", Laura Jana wrote:

> On the one hand, this is a story of how an undeniably quirky teenage boy clings to order, deals with a family crisis, and tries to make sense of the world as he sees it. But it also provides profound insight into a disorder – autism – that leaves those who have it struggling to perceive even the most basic of human emotions. In so doing, _The Curious Incident_ leaves its readers with a greater appreciation of their own ability to feel, express, and interpret emotions. This mainstream literary success made its way to the top of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ bestseller list for fiction at the same time it was being touted by experts in Asperger's syndrome and autism-spectrum disorders as an unrivaled fictional depiction of the inner workings of an autistic teenage boy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-12)

### Metaphor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Metaphor")]

Christopher often comments on his inability to understand or appreciate the concept of [metaphors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphor "Metaphor"). He gives as an example a quote that he found in "a proper novel": "I am veined with iron, with silver, and with streaks of common mud. I cannot contract into the firm fist which those clench who do not depend on stimulus." Haddon told NPR journalist [Terry Gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Gross "Terry Gross"), "Funnily enough, it's actually a quote from [Virginia Woolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Woolf "Virginia Woolf"). It's Virginia Woolf on an off day, in the middle, I think, of _[The Waves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Waves "The Waves")_. An author whom I love actually, but who sometimes got a little too carried away."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-13)

### Multimodality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Multimodality")]

The novel is developed in various [semiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiotics "Semiotics") modes or resources: maps, diagrams, pictures, as well as [smileys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smiley "Smiley"), which are not ornamental but crucial to the understanding of the plot. This means that Haddon's novel can be conceived as [multimodal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimodality "Multimodality").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-14)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical response")]

A 2006 survey in Great Britain, conducted by the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s literacy campaign for [World Book Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Book_Day_(United_Kingdom) "World Book Day (United Kingdom)"), found _Curious Incident_ to be among "the top five happy endings, as voted on by readers" in novels (the others were _[Pride and Prejudice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride\_and\_Prejudice "Pride and Prejudice")_, _[To Kill a Mockingbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Kill\_a\_Mockingbird "To Kill a Mockingbird")_, _[Jane Eyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_Eyre "Jane Eyre")_ and _[Rebecca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca\_(novel) "Rebecca (novel)")_, the last of which _Curious_ outranked).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-25)

_[School Library Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School\_Library\_Journal "School Library Journal")_ praised it as a "rich and poignant novel".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-26) The _[San Jose Mercury News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Jose\_Mercury\_News "San Jose Mercury News")_ said: "Haddon does something audacious here, and he does it superbly. He shows us the way consciousness orders the world, even when the world doesn't want to be ordered", adding that "the great achievement of this novel is that it transcends its obvious cleverness. It's more than an exercise in narrative ingenuity. Filled with humor and pain, it verges on profundity in its examination of those things—customs, habits, language, symbols, daily routines, etc.—that simultaneously unite and separate human beings."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-27) A reviewer for _[The Christian Century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Century "The Christian Century")_ described it as "an absorbing, plausible book": "The reader becomes absorbed not only in the mystery of a murdered dog and a missing mom, but also in the mysterious world of an autistic child."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-28)

A reviewer for _[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlanta\_Journal-Constitution "The Atlanta Journal-Constitution")_ wrote that the story is "a touching evolution, one that Haddon scripts with tenderness and care... a unique window into the mind of a boy who thinks a little differently, but like many kids his age, doesn't quite know how to feel."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-29) Professor Roger Soder called it "visceral" and a "delightful story", declaring, "All of us in our Spokane Book Club are special education professionals and so have considerable experience with kids with this disability, and we found the story believable."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-30)

Cathy Lowne of the _[Encyclopædia Britannica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encyclop%C3%A6dia\_Britannica "Encyclopædia Britannica")_ wrote that "Haddon's skill lies in writing so that, although Christopher may be unaware of emotional undercurrents and nuances of mood, the reader is made aware of them."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-31)

In 2019, the book was ranked 19th on _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s list of the 100 best books of the 21st century.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-32)

### Medical professionals' reviews

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Medical professionals' reviews")]

Alex McClimens, whom Muller quoted above, also wrote: "This magnificent essay in communication is compulsory reading for anyone with the slightest interest in autistic spectrum disorders. This book is also required reading for those who simply enjoy a fascinating story... we are offered a first person narrative to match anything by contemporary writers. Mark Haddon has created a true literary character and his handling of the teenage Asperger's heroic adventure is brilliantly crafted. He uses the literal mind-set of his hero to mask the true direction of the plot."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-33) Reviewer Paul Moorehead calls the book "a fairly ripping adventure story" and writes: "It's also quite a feat of writing. The actual use of language is somewhat austere—an unavoidable consequence of having a boy with autism as a narrator—but it has its own beauty, and it works. So persuasive and so effective is the construction of Christopher, not only is he a character you're rooting for, he's also the character in the story you understand the best. It's startling how believably and comfortably this story puts you into what you might have thought were likely to be some pretty alien shoes."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-34)

Reviewer David Ellis, naming _The Curious Incident_ an "ambitious and innovative novel", wrote that Haddon "manages to avoid the opposing pitfalls of either offending people with autism and their families or turning Christopher into an object of pity. Instead of becoming the focus of the plot the autism enhances it. The unemotional descriptions amplify many moments of observational comedy, and misfortunes are made extremely poignantly." He concludes that Christopher's story is "far more enjoyable and likely to stay with you for far longer than any medical textbook".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-35)

### Challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Challenges")]

_The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time_ has frequently been challenged due to its offensive language, supposed unsuitability for younger readers, and also religious viewpoint.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-admin-36) On the American Library Association's lists of the most banned and challenged books, the book landed in the 51st spot between 2010 and 2019,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-37) and the fifth spot in 2015.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-admin-36)

In 2015 the cast was [Sion Daniel Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sion_Daniel_Young "Sion Daniel Young") as Christopher Boone, with Rebecca Lacey as Siobhan, Nicolas Tennant as Ed, [Mary Stockley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Stockley "Mary Stockley") as Judy, Jacqueline Clarke as Mrs Alexander, Indra Ové as Mrs Shears, [Stephen Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Beckett "Stephen Beckett") as Roger Shears, Matthew Trevannion as Mr Thompson, [Pearl Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Mackie "Pearl Mackie") as No. 40/Punk Girl, Sean McKenzie as Reverend Peters and Kaffe Keating played alternate Christopher. They were joined by Mark Rawlings, Penelope McGhie, Naomi Said and Simon Victor.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-44)

[Mickey Rowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Rowe "Mickey Rowe") was the first openly autistic actor to play Christopher Boone in _The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-46) He documented this experience in the book _Fearlessly Different: An Autistic Actor's Journey to Broadway's Biggest Stage_.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-48)

An adaptation and translation into Spanish by María Renée Prudencio played at the [Teatro de los Insurgentes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_de_los_Insurgentes "Teatro de los Insurgentes") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") in June 2014. The character of Christopher was played by Luis Gerardo Méndez and by Alfonso Dosal on alternate days. An Israeli adaptation (translation into Hebrew by Daniel Efrat) has been staged at the [Beit Lessin Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beit_Lessin_Theater "Beit Lessin Theater") in Tel Aviv since March of the same year, starring Nadav Netz as Christopher; in 2015, Netz won the Best Actor category at the Israeli Theater Awards for his performance.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-49)

An adaptation and translation into French by Dominique Hollier premiered at the [Théâtre de la Tempête](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_de_la_Temp%C3%AAte?action=edit&redlink=1 "Théâtre de la Tempête (page does not exist)") in Paris, directed by [Philippe Adrien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Adrien "Philippe Adrien"), running from September 11 through 18 October 2015. It also ran at Théâtre [Le Moderne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Moderne?action=edit&redlink=1 "Le Moderne (page does not exist)"), in Liege, Belgium, direction by [Daniel Henry-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Henry-Smith?action=edit&redlink=1 "Daniel Henry-Smith (page does not exist)"), from 28 April through 13 May 2017.

An adaptation and translation into Danish by Christian Bundegaard premiered at the Odense Teater, September 2019, starring Kristoffer Helmuth as Christopher.

The production began a 10th anniversary UK & Ireland tour at Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre on 20 November 2021.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Film")]

The film rights for the novel were optioned by [Brad Grey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Grey "Brad Grey") and [Brad Pitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt") for [Warner Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-51) In 2011, [Steve Kloves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kloves "Steve Kloves") was attached to write and direct the project, but as of 2026 it has not yet been produced.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Stanley-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Guardian-53)

A [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language")-English adaptation of the novel has been filmed by Sudipto Roy called _[Kia and Cosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kia\_and\_Cosmos "Kia and Cosmos")_, with the gender roles of the characters reversed, and the plot centering around the killing of a cat called Cosmos.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-54)

_**The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time**_ is a 2003 [mystery novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mystery_novel "Mystery novel") by English writer [Mark Haddon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Haddon "Mark Haddon"). Haddon and _The Curious Incident_ won the [Whitbread Book Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitbread_Book_Awards "Whitbread Book Awards") for Best Novel and Book of the Year,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-costabookawards-1) the [Commonwealth Writers' Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Writers'_Prize "Commonwealth Writers' Prize") for Best First Book,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-vic-2) and the [Guardian Children's Fiction Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guardian_Children's_Fiction_Prize "Guardian Children's Fiction Prize").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-prize2003-3)

Haddon considered this his first novel for adults, as his previous books were for children. Unusually, his publisher also released a separate edition for the children's market, and it was successful there.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Ezard-4)

The novel is narrated in [first-person](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-person_narrative "First-person narrative") by Christopher John Francis Boone, a 15-year-old boy who is described as "a mathematician with some behavioural difficulties" living in [Swindon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon "Swindon"), Wiltshire. Although Christopher's condition is not stated, the book's blurb refers to [Asperger syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asperger_syndrome "Asperger syndrome"). Some commentators have characterized Christopher as on the [autism spectrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autism_spectrum "Autism spectrum").

In July 2009, Haddon wrote on his blog that "_The Curious Incident_ is not a book about Asperger's... if anything it's a novel about difference, about being an outsider, about seeing the world in a surprising and revealing way. The protagonist, being neuro-diverse shows that. The book is not specifically about any specific disorder". Haddon said that he is not an expert on the autism spectrum or Asperger's syndrome.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-mh-autism-5)

He chose to indicate chapters by [prime numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_number "Prime number"), rather than the conventional successive numbers, to express a different world view. Originally written in English, the book has been translated into 36 additional languages.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-translations-6)

The book’s title is a line of [Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock_Holmes "Sherlock Holmes")’ dialogue from the short story "[The Adventure of Silver Blaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Adventure_of_Silver_Blaze "The Adventure of Silver Blaze")" by [Sir Arthur Conan Doyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Conan_Doyle "Arthur Conan Doyle").

## Plot

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Plot")]

In late 1998, Christopher John Francis Boone is a 15-year-old boy living in [Swindon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swindon "Swindon"), England with his widowed father, Ed. One night, Christopher discovers that his neighbour Eileen Shears' dog, Wellington, has been fatally speared with a garden fork. As Christopher mourns over Wellington's body, Eileen calls the police. When a policeman grabs Christopher's arm, Christopher panics and hits him; he is subsequently arrested for assault, though he is quickly released with a caution. Christopher decides to investigate Wellington's death and chronicle his findings in a book, despite Ed's objections. During the investigation, he meets the elderly Mrs. Alexander, who informs Christopher that his late mother Judy was having an affair with Eileen's husband Roger.

Ed discovers the book and confiscates it. While searching Ed's room for the book, Christopher finds letters from Judy, dated after her supposed death. Eventually, he realizes that Judy is still alive and living in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") with Roger. Finding a distressed Christopher in a [catatonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catatonic "Catatonic") state and realizing that he has discovered the letters, Ed admits to lying about Judy's death and confesses to killing Wellington in a fit of anger after an argument with Eileen. Fearing for his own safety, Christopher decides to run away and live with Judy.

After a long, event-filled journey, evading policemen and feeling overwhelmed by the trains and crowds around him, Christopher eventually finds his way to the home of Judy and Roger, much to the delight of the former and chagrin of the latter. Soon after arriving, Christopher requests to return to Swindon to take his mathematics [A-level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-level "A-level"), but Judy contacts the school to postpone it. She and Roger later break up due to the latter's reluctance to accept Christopher. Judy subsequently returns to Swindon with Christopher, and the exam is reinstated.

After an argument, Judy agrees to let Ed see Christopher for brief daily visits. Christopher remains apprehensive of his father, hoping he will be imprisoned for killing Wellington. Ed gifts Christopher a puppy, whom Christopher names Sandy, and promises to gradually regain Christopher's trust. Christopher declares that he will take further exams and attend university. He completes his mathematics A-level with top grades. The book ends with Christopher optimistic about his future.

## Themes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Themes")]

### Social disability

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Social disability")]

In a 2004 interview, Haddon said

> I have to say honestly that I did more research about the London Underground and the inside of Swindon Railway Station, where some of the novel takes place, than I did about Asperger's syndrome. I gave [Christopher] kind of 9 or 10 rules that he would live his life by, and then I didn't read any more about Asperger's because I think there is no typical person who has Asperger's syndrome, and they're as large and diverse a group of people as any other group in society. And the important thing is that I did a lot of imagining, that I did a lot of putting myself into his shoes in trying to make him come alive as a human being rather than getting him right, whatever that might mean.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-NPR-7)

Haddon states on his website that, although he had read "a handful of newspaper and magazine articles about, or by, people with Asperger's and autism" in preparation for writing the book, he knows "very little" about Asperger's syndrome and that Christopher Boone is inspired by two different people. According to Haddon, neither of these people can be labelled as having a disability. Haddon added that he "slightly regret[s]" that the term _Asperger's syndrome_ appeared on the cover of his novel.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-mh-autism-5) In 2010, in an interview with _[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Independent "The Independent")_, he was described as

> now thoroughly irritated that the word Asperger's appeared on subsequent editions of the novel, because now everyone imagines that he is an expert and he keeps getting phone calls asking him to appear at lectures.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Independent-8)

In a critical essay on the novel, Vivienne Muller quotes some praise by experts on [disability theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disability#Theory "Disability"):

> In its presentation of Christopher's everyday experiences of the society in which he lives, the narrative offers a rich canvas of experiences for an ethnographic study of this particular cognitive condition, and one which places a positive spin on the syndrome. The reader in this instance acts as ethnographer, invited to see what Mark Osteen claims is a 'quality in autistic lives that is valuable in and of itself'.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-9) Along similar lines, [Alex] McClimens writes that Haddon's novel is 'an ethnographic delight' and that 'Haddon's achievement is to have written a novel that turns on the central character's difference without making that difference a stigmatising characteristic.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-10)

Muller adds that the novel

> works with a strong sense of the disabled speaking subject, drawing readers into Christopher's cognitive / corporeal space through an incremental layering of his perspectives and reactions... The narrative also bristles with diagrams, maps, drawings, stories, texts that inform Christopher's lexicon for mapping meaning in a world of bewildering signs and sounds.

She also admires such elements as

> the digressive stream-of-connectedness-and-disconnectedness way in which Christopher writes and thinks; the obsessive focus on minutiae; his musings about why animals behave the way they do; his quasi-philosophizing on death and life and the afterlife; his ambition to be an astronaut...[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-11)

In a survey of children's books which "teach about emotional life", Laura Jana wrote:

> On the one hand, this is a story of how an undeniably quirky teenage boy clings to order, deals with a family crisis, and tries to make sense of the world as he sees it. But it also provides profound insight into a disorder – autism – that leaves those who have it struggling to perceive even the most basic of human emotions. In so doing, _The Curious Incident_ leaves its readers with a greater appreciation of their own ability to feel, express, and interpret emotions. This mainstream literary success made its way to the top of _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ bestseller list for fiction at the same time it was being touted by experts in Asperger's syndrome and autism-spectrum disorders as an unrivaled fictional depiction of the inner workings of an autistic teenage boy.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-12)

### Metaphor

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Metaphor")]

Christopher often comments on his inability to understand or appreciate the concept of [metaphors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metaphor "Metaphor"). He gives as an example a quote that he found in "a proper novel": "I am veined with iron, with silver, and with streaks of common mud. I cannot contract into the firm fist which those clench who do not depend on stimulus." Haddon told NPR journalist [Terry Gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Gross "Terry Gross"), "Funnily enough, it's actually a quote from [Virginia Woolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Woolf "Virginia Woolf"). It's Virginia Woolf on an off day, in the middle, I think, of _[The Waves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Waves "The Waves")_. An author whom I love actually, but who sometimes got a little too carried away."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-13)

### Multimodality

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Multimodality")]

The novel is developed in various [semiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semiotics "Semiotics") modes or resources: maps, diagrams, pictures, as well as [smileys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smiley "Smiley"), which are not ornamental but crucial to the understanding of the plot. This means that Haddon's novel can be conceived as [multimodal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multimodality "Multimodality").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-14)

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Critical response")]

A 2006 survey in Great Britain, conducted by the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")'s literacy campaign for [World Book Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Book_Day_(United_Kingdom) "World Book Day (United Kingdom)"), found _Curious Incident_ to be among "the top five happy endings, as voted on by readers" in novels (the others were _[Pride and Prejudice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pride\_and\_Prejudice "Pride and Prejudice")_, _[To Kill a Mockingbird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/To\_Kill\_a\_Mockingbird "To Kill a Mockingbird")_, _[Jane Eyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane\_Eyre "Jane Eyre")_ and _[Rebecca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rebecca\_(novel) "Rebecca (novel)")_, the last of which _Curious_ outranked).[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-25)

_[School Library Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School\_Library\_Journal "School Library Journal")_ praised it as a "rich and poignant novel".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-26) The _[San Jose Mercury News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San\_Jose\_Mercury\_News "San Jose Mercury News")_ said: "Haddon does something audacious here, and he does it superbly. He shows us the way consciousness orders the world, even when the world doesn't want to be ordered", adding that "the great achievement of this novel is that it transcends its obvious cleverness. It's more than an exercise in narrative ingenuity. Filled with humor and pain, it verges on profundity in its examination of those things—customs, habits, language, symbols, daily routines, etc.—that simultaneously unite and separate human beings."[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-27) A reviewer for _[The Christian Century](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Christian\_Century "The Christian Century")_ described it as "an absorbing, plausible book": "The reader becomes absorbed not only in the mystery of a murdered dog and a missing mom, but also in the mysterious world of an autistic child."[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-28)

A reviewer for _[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlanta\_Journal-Constitution "The Atlanta Journal-Constitution")_ wrote that the story is "a touching evolution, one that Haddon scripts with tenderness and care... a unique window into the mind of a boy who thinks a little differently, but like many kids his age, doesn't quite know how to feel."[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-29) Professor Roger Soder called it "visceral" and a "delightful story", declaring, "All of us in our Spokane Book Club are special education professionals and so have considerable experience with kids with this disability, and we found the story believable."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-30)

Cathy Lowne of the _[Encyclopædia Britannica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Encyclop%C3%A6dia\_Britannica "Encyclopædia Britannica")_ wrote that "Haddon's skill lies in writing so that, although Christopher may be unaware of emotional undercurrents and nuances of mood, the reader is made aware of them."[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-31)

In 2019, the book was ranked 19th on _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_'s list of the 100 best books of the 21st century.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-32)

### Medical professionals' reviews

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Medical professionals' reviews")]

Alex McClimens, whom Muller quoted above, also wrote: "This magnificent essay in communication is compulsory reading for anyone with the slightest interest in autistic spectrum disorders. This book is also required reading for those who simply enjoy a fascinating story... we are offered a first person narrative to match anything by contemporary writers. Mark Haddon has created a true literary character and his handling of the teenage Asperger's heroic adventure is brilliantly crafted. He uses the literal mind-set of his hero to mask the true direction of the plot."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-33) Reviewer Paul Moorehead calls the book "a fairly ripping adventure story" and writes: "It's also quite a feat of writing. The actual use of language is somewhat austere—an unavoidable consequence of having a boy with autism as a narrator—but it has its own beauty, and it works. So persuasive and so effective is the construction of Christopher, not only is he a character you're rooting for, he's also the character in the story you understand the best. It's startling how believably and comfortably this story puts you into what you might have thought were likely to be some pretty alien shoes."[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-34)

Reviewer David Ellis, naming _The Curious Incident_ an "ambitious and innovative novel", wrote that Haddon "manages to avoid the opposing pitfalls of either offending people with autism and their families or turning Christopher into an object of pity. Instead of becoming the focus of the plot the autism enhances it. The unemotional descriptions amplify many moments of observational comedy, and misfortunes are made extremely poignantly." He concludes that Christopher's story is "far more enjoyable and likely to stay with you for far longer than any medical textbook".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-35)

### Challenges

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Challenges")]

_The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time_ has frequently been challenged due to its offensive language, supposed unsuitability for younger readers, and also religious viewpoint.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-admin-36) On the American Library Association's lists of the most banned and challenged books, the book landed in the 51st spot between 2010 and 2019,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-37) and the fifth spot in 2015.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-admin-36)

In 2015 the cast was [Sion Daniel Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sion_Daniel_Young "Sion Daniel Young") as Christopher Boone, with Rebecca Lacey as Siobhan, Nicolas Tennant as Ed, [Mary Stockley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Stockley "Mary Stockley") as Judy, Jacqueline Clarke as Mrs Alexander, Indra Ové as Mrs Shears, [Stephen Beckett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Beckett "Stephen Beckett") as Roger Shears, Matthew Trevannion as Mr Thompson, [Pearl Mackie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Mackie "Pearl Mackie") as No. 40/Punk Girl, Sean McKenzie as Reverend Peters and Kaffe Keating played alternate Christopher. They were joined by Mark Rawlings, Penelope McGhie, Naomi Said and Simon Victor.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-44)

[Mickey Rowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Rowe "Mickey Rowe") was the first openly autistic actor to play Christopher Boone in _The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-46) He documented this experience in the book _Fearlessly Different: An Autistic Actor's Journey to Broadway's Biggest Stage_.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-48)

An adaptation and translation into Spanish by María Renée Prudencio played at the [Teatro de los Insurgentes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_de_los_Insurgentes "Teatro de los Insurgentes") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") in June 2014. The character of Christopher was played by Luis Gerardo Méndez and by Alfonso Dosal on alternate days. An Israeli adaptation (translation into Hebrew by Daniel Efrat) has been staged at the [Beit Lessin Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beit_Lessin_Theater "Beit Lessin Theater") in Tel Aviv since March of the same year, starring Nadav Netz as Christopher; in 2015, Netz won the Best Actor category at the Israeli Theater Awards for his performance.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-49)

An adaptation and translation into French by Dominique Hollier premiered at the [Théâtre de la Tempête](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Th%C3%A9%C3%A2tre_de_la_Temp%C3%AAte?action=edit&redlink=1 "Théâtre de la Tempête (page does not exist)") in Paris, directed by [Philippe Adrien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Adrien "Philippe Adrien"), running from September 11 through 18 October 2015. It also ran at Théâtre [Le Moderne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Le_Moderne?action=edit&redlink=1 "Le Moderne (page does not exist)"), in Liege, Belgium, direction by [Daniel Henry-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Henry-Smith?action=edit&redlink=1 "Daniel Henry-Smith (page does not exist)"), from 28 April through 13 May 2017.

An adaptation and translation into Danish by Christian Bundegaard premiered at the Odense Teater, September 2019, starring Kristoffer Helmuth as Christopher.

The production began a 10th anniversary UK & Ireland tour at Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre on 20 November 2021.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Film")]

The film rights for the novel were optioned by [Brad Grey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Grey "Brad Grey") and [Brad Pitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brad_Pitt "Brad Pitt") for [Warner Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-51) In 2011, [Steve Kloves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kloves "Steve Kloves") was attached to write and direct the project, but as of 2026 it has not yet been produced.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Stanley-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-Guardian-53)

A [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_language "Bengali language")-English adaptation of the novel has been filmed by Sudipto Roy called _[Kia and Cosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kia\_and\_Cosmos "Kia and Cosmos")_, with the gender roles of the characters reversed, and the plot centering around the killing of a cat called Cosmos.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Curious_Incident_of_the_Dog_in_the_Night-Time#cite_note-54)

**Johns Hopkins University** (often abbreviated as **Johns Hopkins**, **Hopkins**, or **JHU**) is a [private](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_university "Private university")[research university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university "Research university") in [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore"), Maryland, United States. Incorporated in 1867 and opened in 1876 based on the European research institution model, Johns Hopkins is considered to be the first research university in the U.S.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-9)

The university was named for its first benefactor, the American businessman and [Quaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quakers "Quakers") philanthropist [Johns Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins "Johns Hopkins").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-There_is_only_one_Johns_Hopkins-10) Hopkins's $7 million bequest (equivalent to $166 million in 2024)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-inflation-USGDP-11) to establish the university and the affiliated [Johns Hopkins Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_Hospital "Johns Hopkins Hospital") in Baltimore was the largest [philanthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philanthropy "Philanthropy") gift in U.S. history up to that time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Facts_at_a_Glance-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-racial_record-13)[Daniel Coit Gilman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Coit_Gilman "Daniel Coit Gilman"), who was inaugurated as [Johns Hopkins's first president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:Presidents_of_Johns_Hopkins_University "Category:Presidents of Johns Hopkins University") on February 22, 1876,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Inaugural_Address_of_Daniel_Coit_Gilman-14) led the university to revolutionize higher education in the U.S. by integrating teaching and research.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Benson_Page_x-15) In 1900, Johns Hopkins became a founding member of the [Association of American Universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_of_American_Universities "Association of American Universities").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-16) The [School of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Medicine "Johns Hopkins School of Medicine"), established in 1893, has achieved international recognition for its pioneering biomedical research.

The university consists of ten academic divisions mostly divided among four campuses in Baltimore, with some graduate campuses in [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy"), [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-17) The university's two undergraduate divisions, the [Zanvyl Krieger School of Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zanvyl_Krieger_School_of_Arts_and_Sciences "Zanvyl Krieger School of Arts and Sciences") and the [Whiting School of Engineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whiting_School_of_Engineering "Whiting School of Engineering"), are located on the [Homewood campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homewood_Campus_of_Johns_Hopkins_University "Homewood Campus of Johns Hopkins University") adjacent to Baltimore's [Charles Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Village,_Baltimore "Charles Village, Baltimore") neighborhood.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-homewoodcampus-18) The [School of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Medicine "Johns Hopkins School of Medicine"), [School of Nursing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Nursing "Johns Hopkins School of Nursing"), and [Bloomberg School of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloomberg_School_of_Public_Health "Bloomberg School of Public Health") are located on the medical campus in East Baltimore, alongside Johns Hopkins Hospital.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-eastbaltimorecampus-19) The university also consists of the [Peabody Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peabody_Institute "Peabody Institute") in Baltimore's [Mount Vernon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Vernon,_Baltimore "Mount Vernon, Baltimore") neighborhood, [Applied Physics Laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Applied_Physics_Laboratory "Applied Physics Laboratory") in [Howard County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_County,_Maryland "Howard County, Maryland"), [School of Advanced International Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_of_Advanced_International_Studies "School of Advanced International Studies"), [School of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Education "Johns Hopkins School of Education"), and [Carey Business School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carey_Business_School "Carey Business School").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-hopkinscampuses-20)

Founded in 1883, the [Johns Hopkins Blue Jays men's lacrosse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_Blue_Jays_men's_lacrosse "Johns Hopkins Blue Jays men's lacrosse") team, which is an affiliate member in the [Big Ten Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Ten_Conference "Big Ten Conference"), has won 44 national titles.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-22) The university's other sports teams compete in [Division III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_III "NCAA Division III") of the [NCAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Collegiate_Athletic_Association "National Collegiate Athletic Association"), where they are members of the [Centennial Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centennial_Conference "Centennial Conference").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Johns_Hopkins_University&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Philanthropic beginnings and foundation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Johns_Hopkins_University&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Philanthropic beginnings and foundation")]

Further information: [Humboldtian model of higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humboldtian_model_of_higher_education "Humboldtian model of higher education") and [Johns Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins "Johns Hopkins")

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Hopkinsp.jpg/250px-Hopkinsp.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hopkinsp.jpg)

[Johns Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins "Johns Hopkins"), the university's namesake whose philanthropic gift in 1873 established the university, [Johns Hopkins Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_Hospital "Johns Hopkins Hospital"), and the [Johns Hopkins School of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_School_of_Medicine "Johns Hopkins School of Medicine")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Heidelberg_Universit%C3%A4tsbibliothek_2003_b.jpg/250px-Heidelberg_Universit%C3%A4tsbibliothek_2003_b.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Heidelberg_Universit%C3%A4tsbibliothek_2003_b.jpg)

The university model of [Heidelberg University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg_University "Heidelberg University") in [Heidelberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg "Heidelberg"), Germany, was replicated in the founding of Johns Hopkins University

On his death in 1873, [Johns Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins "Johns Hopkins"), a [Quaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quakers "Quakers") businessman and childless bachelor, bequeathed $7 million (equivalent to $166 million in 2024)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-inflation-USGDP-11) to fund a hospital and university in [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-HC-23)

At the time, this donation, generated primarily from the [Baltimore and Ohio Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_and_Ohio_Railroad "Baltimore and Ohio Railroad"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Who_Was_Johns_Hopkins?-24) was the largest philanthropic gift in the history of the United States,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Facts_at_a_Glance-12) and endowment was then the largest in America.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-racial_record-13)

Hopkins’s relationship to slavery has been the subject of historical debate. In 2020, research commissioned by the university, and led by historian [Martha S. Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_S._Jones "Martha S. Jones"), cited 1840 and 1850 census records as evidence that individuals recorded as enslaved were his property and associated with his household.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-26) Subsequent scholarship has questioned this interpretation, noting the limitations of census data, particularly the ambiguity of the 1850 slave schedule, and the absence of corroborating documentation such as tax or probate records linking Hopkins directly to slaveholding.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-27)

The first name of philanthropist Johns Hopkins comes from the surname of his great-grandmother, Margaret Johns, who married Gerard Hopkins.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Who_Was_Johns_Hopkins?-24) They named last their son Johns Hopkins, who named his son Samuel Hopkins. Samuel named one of his sons for his father, and that son became the university's benefactor. [Milton Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Eisenhower "Milton Eisenhower"), a former university president, once spoke at a convention in [Pittsburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pittsburgh "Pittsburgh") where the [master of ceremonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_ceremonies "Master of ceremonies") introduced him as "President of _John_ Hopkins". Eisenhower retorted that he was "glad to be here in _Pitt_ burgh".[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-Cheesecake_on_the_Tart_Side-28)

The original board opted for an entirely novel university model dedicated to the discovery of knowledge at an advanced level, extending that of contemporary Germany.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-muller-29) Building on the [Humboldtian model of higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humboldtian_model_of_higher_education "Humboldtian model of higher education"), the [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") education model of [Wilhelm von Humboldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_von_Humboldt "Wilhelm von Humboldt"), it became dedicated to research. It was especially [Heidelberg University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heidelberg_University "Heidelberg University") and its long academic research history on which the new institution tried to model itself.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-muller-29)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Johns Hopkins thereby became the model of the modern research university in the United States. Its success eventually shifted higher education in the United States from a focus on teaching revealed and/or applied knowledge to the scientific discovery of new knowledge.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johns_Hopkins_University#cite_note-30)
